title: Flip one bit of the message
hook: Change a message by a single bit. How much of its SHA-256 hash moves?

knows: a hash maps data to a fixed-size output
letters are stored as 8 bits each
doesNotKnow: that a good hash output looks unrelated after a tiny input change (the avalanche effect)

misconception: Similar inputs give similar hashes, so a hash is a rough fingerprint of the content.
objective: The learner can explain that flipping one input bit changes about half (about 128 of 256) of SHA-256's output bits, so similar messages get unrelated hashes and a message cannot be nudged toward a target hash.

claims.text: SHA-256 turns any message into 256 bits.
claims.source: NIST FIPS 180-4, Secure Hash Standard (2015), section 6.2: SHA-256 message digest is 256 bits.

claims.text: Flipping one bit of the message changes about half of the 256 output bits, about 128 on average, not a handful.
claims.source: Builder ran 1,000 random one-bit flips of random 3-byte messages through sha256.ts in Node: mean 127.7 changed bits, min 103, max 157. On the stage's QA path (bits 1-16 of 'cat', flipped in turn) the counts were 129, 112, 129, 131, 137, 122, 135, 123, 127, 125, 127, 136, 117, 132, 127, 126.

claims.text: The stage computes a real SHA-256 of the 3-letter message (8 bits per letter) on every tap.
claims.source: sha256.ts in the lesson folder. Builder checked: 'abc' gives ba7816bf8f01cfea414140de5dae2223b00361a396177a9cb410ff61f20015ad (FIPS 180-4 example) and 200 further inputs match Node's crypto.createHash('sha256'). Letters are ASCII bytes ('c' = 0x63).

claims.text: A good hash is built so that each output bit flips with a chance of about one half, like a coin toss, when any input bit changes.
claims.source: Strict avalanche criterion: Webster and Tavares, 'On the Design of S-Boxes', CRYPTO '85. Expected 256 x 1/2 = 128 matches c2's simulation. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Strict avalanche criterion, Webster & Tavares, 'On the Design of S-Boxes', CRYPTO '85, LNCS 218:523-534 (citation confirmed by web search). Own node check with node:crypto SHA-256 (fc1/aval.mjs): 71,120 single-bit flips of 2,000 messages, each of the 256 output bits flipped with frequency 0.494 to 0.505; mean 128.03 bits changed. Stage says 'whenever anything in the message changes', slightly broader than SAC, but true of SHA-256 in practice.

claims.text: So similar messages do not get similar hashes, and a message cannot be nudged toward a chosen hash bit by bit.
claims.source: Preimage resistance as a design goal of SHA-2: NIST SP 800-107 Rev. 1 (2012), section 4.1; the avalanche result (c2) is why small edits give no partial progress. Stated as a design property, not a proof. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Same script: a one-bit edit changes 94 to 170 of 256 bits (mean 128), the same as two unrelated digests, so similarity in the message carries no similarity in the hash and no single edit moves the digest only a little; preimage resistance (NIST glossary, citing SP 800-107 Rev. 1) is the design goal. I could not open SP 800-107 (NIST host blocked) to confirm 'section 4.1'; the property is confirmed, the section number is not. Stated as a design property, not a proof.

claims.text: A hash is a fixed-size fingerprint of a message, used to check that it was not altered. A dot (·) on the stage stands for a byte with no printable character, or a space: any byte outside 33 to 126.
claims.source: Standard definition of a cryptographic hash function (NIST FIPS 180-4 for SHA-256: message digest used to detect changes). | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 19): Sentence 1 holds (FIPS 180-4: a digest used to detect whether a message changed). Sentence 2 does not match the code: charOf shows bytes 33-126 as themselves and · only for bytes outside that range. Node: the 24 one-bit flips of 'cat' give # ! ` 4 | (non-letters, shown as themselves) and · only when the top bit is set. So · is not 'a character that is not a printable letter', and the stage label '· is a non-letter symbol' is wrong too. Fix (builder, claim and Demo.tsx label): '· stands for a byte with no printable character'. | v2 (2026-10-14, builder): sentence 2 and the stage label reworded per pass 19 to match charOf (bytes 33-126 shown as themselves, all others as ·; a space, byte 32, can be reached by flipping two bits and also shows as ·). Previous verdict void; needs re-check. | FACT-CHECK 2026-10-14 (pass 20): charOf(v) at Demo.tsx line 22 returns the character for 33..126 and '·' otherwise; stage label line 78 says '· stands for a byte with no printable character, or a space', matching the claim (32 is space, 0-31 and 127 control, 128-255 none in ASCII). Sentence 1 as pass 19 (FIPS 180-4). The question text repeats sentence 1.

recall.question: Two files differ in a single character. You compare their SHA-256 hashes bit by bit. What do you expect?
options: About half of the bits differ
recall.why: A good hash makes every output bit flip with about a coin-toss chance when anything changes, so about 128 of 256 bits differ: the hashes look unrelated.
